result.notes:
Implemented per lib/letflow/design/req157-lua-capability-model.md. `Letflow.Engine.Lua.Capabilities` (new) holds grant_set()/denial() per design §2 exactly: new/0, new/1, add/2, has?/2, check/3, check!/3, service_capability/1. `Letflow.Engine.Lua.Platform` extended with the 8-row capability matrix (design §4.1), install/2 as the single fold-based registration point (INV-CAP-1), install/1 reduced to `install(lua, Capabilities.new())`, the 6 not-yet-implemented stubs plus now/fail (design §4.3), and moduledoc content covering the full matrix and the now/fail ungated rationale + binding statement (design §5) -- verified both by a new REQ-157 moduledoc-content test group and by the pre-existing REQ-152 moduledoc tests, which still pass unmodified.

DEVIATION FROM DESIGN (flagged, not silently made): design §4.1's `matrix_row` type specifies `required`/`stub` as raw Elixir closures (`required_capability_fun()`/`stub_fun()`) stored directly on `@capability_matrix`. Elixir module attributes cannot hold anonymous functions -- only literal/escapable terms (confirmed by a real compile error: `ArgumentError ... cannot inject attribute @capability_matrix into function/macro because cannot escape #Function<...>. The supported values are: lists, tuples, maps, atoms, numbers, bitstrings, PIDs and remote functions in the format &Mod.fun/arity`). Represented `required`/`stub` as plain data tags instead (`:none | :call_service_arg0 | <capability string>` and `:now | :fail | :not_yet_implemented`), resolved by two small private dispatch functions (`required_capability/2`, `run_stub/3`) called from inside `install/2`'s fold. `@capability_matrix` itself remains a single literal module attribute with exactly 8 rows; `install/2` remains the one and only call site under lib/ that calls `Lua.set!(lua_acc, [:platform, _], _)` (INV-CAP-1, verified by a source-level regex test). No behavior differs from the design's intent -- this is purely how the per-row function is represented internally. Flagging for REVIEWER per this role's 'don't silently re-decide' rule.
